title: State update after a statement
statement: A state consists of an integer-valued location map and an integer-valued memory map, both indexed by natural numbers. Define the state after executing a statement as follows: a skip, procedure call, or while statement leaves the state unchanged; an assignment updates the specified location with the expression’s value in the original state, and a store updates the memory cell whose index is the natural-number conversion of the address expression’s value, storing the value of the other expression. A sequence applies its first statement and then its second, while a conditional applies the branch selected by whether its condition holds in the original state.
